title: Universal In-Plane Confined Growth of Mesoporous Metal–Organic Framework Crystalline Heterostructures
abstract: Abstract Constructing mesoporous MOF heterostructures on conductive two-dimensional hosts remains challenging because interfacial contact and pore accessibility are rarely optimized simultaneously. Herein, we report a universal in-plane confined growth strategy for mesoporous UiO-66-NH2/MXene heterostructures featuring continuous interfacial contact and vertically accessible mesochannels. In contrast to conventional particle-on-sheet hybrids, the resulting architecture enables improved electrolyte penetration, shortened Zn2+ transport pathways, and efficient interfacial electron transfer. By regulating micellar assembly at the interface, an optimal mesostructural regime is identified in which ion accessibility and structural confinement are best balanced. Consequently, the optimized heterostructure delivers a high energy density of 163.9 Wh kg–1, excellent rate capability (∼68% retention over a 50-fold current increase), and ∼100% capacity retention over 50,000 cycles. Kinetic analyses and ex situ studies further show that the interfacial mesoporous architecture suppresses diffusion limitations and preserves structural integrity during Zn2+ storage. Moreover, the assembly concept shows transferability across substrates of different dimensionalities, highlighting its broader utility for constructing mesoporous crystalline heterostructures. This work provides an effective route to mesoporous MOF heterostructures and a generalizable design principle for hybrid crystalline electrodes.

title: Review and Outlook on Biomass-Derived Carbon Materials and Their Functional Composites with 2D Materials for Sustainable Energy Storage Applications
abstract: Abstract The synergistic integration of sustainable biomass-derived carbon frameworks with highly conductive two-dimensional MXenes represents a promising frontier for bridging the energy–power gap in electrochemical energy-storage systems. This Review highlights the critical role of MXenes, transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), and metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), along with their composites with biomass-derived activated carbon, in designing advanced electrodes for energy storage systems. Biomass-derived carbons offer renewable, low-cost, and hierarchically porous structures that facilitate efficient ion transport, while MXenes provide exceptional electrical conductivity and surface functionality. Meanwhile, MOFs and TMDs introduce tunable porosity and abundant redox-active sites, enabling enhanced pseudocapacitive and Faradaic charge storage. A central focus of this Review is the influence of synthesis strategies on structural evolution and electrochemical performance. Various synthesis approaches are critically discussed to demonstrate how they can tailor three-dimensional architectures, interfacial interactions, and pore distribution, thereby directly influencing key performance metrics, such as specific capacitance, energy density, rate capability, and cycling stability. In addition, the Review comprehensively examines essential characterization techniques and practical performance parameters, including scalability, oxidation stability, and electrolyte compatibility, providing insights into the realistic evaluation of device performance. Finally, future research directions are outlined with an emphasis on green and scalable synthesis routes, flexible and wearable device integration, and the development of electrically efficient and structurally robust architectures. This Review provides a comprehensive framework for the design of next-generation hybrid materials, paving the way for high-performance, sustainable, and commercially viable energy storage technologies.

title: Versatile Interfacial Engineering of Core–Shell Mesoporous Nanomaterials: Programmable Assembly, Functional Integration, and Diverse Applications
abstract: Abstract Integrating diverse building blocks into functional materials with tailored architectures and properties has emerged as an efficient strategy to address the demands of multifunctional applications, and core–shell mesoporous materials (CSMMs) enable the modular integration of functional components and the structural optimization of mass transfer. Enabled by multi-interface nanoassembly strategies, diverse CSMMs have been engineered and sparked intense interdisciplinary interest owing to their distinctive features, including multicomponent synergistic effects, interfacial coupling effects, and rationally designed heterogeneous architectures. Herein, this review systematically introduces the concept of “micellar coating chemistry” and summarizes current assembly strategies for the tailored synthesis of CSMMs. The rational design of structure (e.g. surface roughness, cavity, pore size, and porosity) and composition (e.g. magnetic-, noble metal-, silica-, polymer-, and carbon-based components) are highlighted. Furthermore, functionality integration (e.g. nanoparticle loading, hybridization, and surface functionalization) is also evaluated and summarized, and the diverse applications of these materials in hot fields, such as catalysis, gas sensing, environmental remediation, biomedicine, energy storage and conversion, are critically assessed and compared. This review outlines future research opportunities and challenges, and establishes a conceptual foundation for the rational design, scalable synthesis, and versatile interdisciplinary applications of CSMMs.

title: Sequential Electrochemical Construction of Hierarchical LIG/PPy/MnO2 Microsupercapacitors with High Areal Capacitance and Device-Level Stability
abstract: Abstract Achieving high areal energy storage in flexible microsupercapacitors while maintaining compatibility with direct planar patterning remains challenging, particularly when multiple pseudocapacitive components must be sequentially integrated without compromising electrode accessibility or device level performance. In this paper, we develop a sequential electrochemical construction strategy to integrate polypyrrole (PPy) and manganese dioxide (MnO2) directly onto interdigitated laser-induced graphene (LIG) electrodes without preformed composite powders, slurry casting, or polymer binders. Porous LIG serves as the conductive framework and current collector, followed by in situ PPy electropolymerization and subsequent MnO2 electrodeposition. Systematic control of LIG processing, PPy growth, MnO2 deposition, and gel electrolyte composition establishes a fabrication window that balances electrical conductivity, pseudocapacitive material loading, and structural accessibility while preserving the underlying porous LIG architecture. Stepwise LIG, LIG/PPy, and LIG/PPy/MnO2 controls exhibit the same performance hierarchy at both the individual electrode and complete device levels, demonstrating that the electrochemical gains introduced during sequential functionalization are retained after complete microsupercapacitor (MSC) assembly. The resulting LIG/PPy/MnO2 device delivers an areal capacitance of 621.2 mF cm–2 at 0.37 mA cm–2 and a maximum areal energy density of 55.22 μWh cm–2 at 0.1494 mW cm–2. Extended rate measurements further demonstrate continued electrochemical operation up to 5 mA cm–2 under substantially increased current demand. The device retains 97.04% of its flat state capacitance at 180° static bending, exhibits a device-to-device RSD of 2.29%, retains 94.5% capacitance after 60 days of ambient storage, and maintains 85.1% after 5000 GCD cycles. Series integration further extends the operating voltage from 0.8 to 2.4 V with predictable electrical scaling and enables three MSCs to power a red LED for approximately 183 s. These results establish a directly patterned and independently controlled approach for translating hierarchical pseudocapacitive construction into high areal energy storage, reproducible device performance, and scalable voltage output.

title: Porous Framework Assembly Creates Functional Tertiary Folds in Small Peptides
abstract: Abstract There is significant interest in recreating the protein tertiary structure in simpler systems, which can enable the precise and modular organization of multiple functional groups for enhancing molecular recognition and catalysis. Small peptides are minimalist analogs of proteins; however, their limited size highly disfavors folding into tertiary structures, especially those that also possess open binding sites needed for function. Here, we report that 3-dimensional self-assembly into a porous crystalline framework overcomes this limitation, producing modular tertiary structures in peptides shorter than 20 amino acids with tunable binding sites. As shown by X-ray crystallography, this framework-mediated folding tolerates many sequences with a broad range of functional groups, and it generates precise confined environments that are dynamic and mutationally robust. Thus, these pores can be programmed to selectively bind complex molecular guests such as nucleotides and perfluoroalkyl substances through the cooperative engagement of up to 10 distinct residues. These results demonstrate that a well-defined tertiary structure can exist in very short peptides and can impart tunable protein-like function to synthetic porous materials.

title: Over 95% Optical Reflectance From Structurally Modulated All‐Biopolymer Multilayers
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable photonics aims to replace conventional optical materials with environmentally benign alternatives, yet its development is fundamentally constrained by the narrow intrinsic refractive‐index variability of biopolymers. Here we show that a dense–porous periodic architecture yields nearly perfect optical reflection using only polysaccharides. By exploiting the difference in skeletal rigidity between amorphous pectin and crystalline cellulose nanofibers (CNFs), we form alternating dense, high‐refractive‐index pectin layers and porous, low‐refractive‐index CNF layers through a combination of electrodeposition with solvent exchange. This dense–porous periodic architecture yields reflectivities exceeding 97% in the visible range and 95% in the near‐infrared—a range unprecedented for biopolymer‐based optical materials. Moreover, the strategy is simple, scalable, and highly versatile, enabling free spectral design across the visible and near‐infrared regions, broadband metallic‐like reflection, and planar patterning within a single fabrication process. Combined with the low thermal conductivity arising from porous layers and the coexistence of visible transparency and near‐infrared reflection, the resulting films show potential as transparent thermal‐management materials. This work establishes a new materials design principle for biodegradable, polysaccharide‐based photonic systems and advances the field of sustainable photonics.

title: Charge-Transfer Engineering Controls Excited-State Dynamics and Supramolecular Assembly in Luminescent Au(I) Complexes
abstract: Abstract Coupling excited-state control with supramolecular self-assembly within a single molecular design remains a central challenge in luminescent materials chemistry. Here, we explore charge-transfer (CT) engineering as a strategy to address both features in a family of luminescent Au(I) bisphosphine complexes. Homoleptic derivatives bearing pyrene, phenanthrene, or triphenylene chromophores were compared with a heteroleptic pyrene/phenanthrene complex designed to promote interchromophoric electronic communication. The homoleptic complexes display predominantly room-temperature fluorescence, with increasing phosphorescence contributions associated with progressive metal perturbation of the excited states. In the heteroleptic complex, the combination of electronically differentiated chromophores enables access to a T2-mediated pathway that promotes room-temperature pyrene phosphorescence, as supported by solvent-dependent photophysical measurements and theoretical calculations. Addition of [Au(CN)2]− enhances fluorescence in all cases, with a 6-fold increase for the heteroleptic complex, and promotes its organization into extended luminescent wires driven by a combination of C–H···N≡C hydrogen bonding and π···π stacking interactions. These results show how chromophore differentiation within an Au(I) coordination scaffold can couple excited-state modulation with supramolecular organization, providing a design strategy for responsive luminescent assemblies.

title: Supramolecular Polymer Nanoparticles for Polymer Toughening
abstract: Abstract Nanoparticle toughening of polymers has long been constrained by the inherent trade-off between strength and toughness. Here, we report a supramolecular polymer nanoparticle toughening strategy based on an H2G2-type monomer (H2G2-1). During epoxy curing, H2G2-1 undergoes in situ self-assembly into supramolecular polymer nanoparticles (H2G2-NPs), which serve dual roles: acting as physical cross-linking points for reinforcement, while their reversible host–guest interactions function as sacrificial bonds that dissociate under stress to dissipate energy. This strategy ensures uniform nanoparticle dispersion and excellent interfacial compatibility. Compared to neat epoxy, the H2G2-NPs-toughened epoxy exhibits a 92.6% increase in elongation at break, a 66.0% increase in tensile strength, and a 233% increase in toughness, achieving synergistic strengthening and toughening. This work provides a new strategy to make high-performance toughened polymers.

title: Synergistic Dual-Fuel-Driven Dissipative (Opto-)Electronic Crystals: Unraveling Spatiotemporal Multifunctionality Beyond Equilibrium
abstract: Abstract Living systems sustain complex far-from-equilibrium structures through the continuous consumption of high-energy chemical fuels, a phenomenon known as dissipative self-assembly (DSA). While DSA has enabled the design of adaptive amorphous materials driven by a single fuel source, the construction of dissipative (opto-)electronic crystals utilizing different fuel inputs acting simultaneously remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a strategy for constructing out-of-equilibrium (opto-)electronic crystals driven by synergetic dual-fuel inputs (chemical and light). Using a bio-organic NG building block, chemical fuel consumption induces a transient condensation reaction that orchestrates successive hydration states of DSA, including colloidal particles and the formation of chiral crystals. Remarkably, the resulting dissipative crystals exhibit light-triggered transient generation of radical anions, providing an additional level of spatiotemporal regulation. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal the atomistic assembly features underlying the various states of the DSA process. Notably, this dual-fuel DSA platform endows the materials with spatiotemporally programmable multifunctionality, enabling self-erasable writing, Boolean-logic-based out-of-equilibrium patterning, and dissipative (opto-)electronic device properties. These findings establish a route toward life-like programmable molecular materials with adaptive responses and autonomous information-processing capabilities, offering new opportunities for smart materials and sustainable (opto-)electronic technologies.

title: Programmable Directional Assembly of Hydrogen-Bonded Lead Organic Chalcogenolates
abstract: Abstract Controlling the directional assembly of metal organic chalcogenolates (MOCs) with atomic precision remains a synthetic challenge yet represents a critical step toward advancing their programmable syntheses and property investigations. Herein, we present a “hydrogen-bond-directed assembly” strategy to drive the formation of single-crystalline, hydrogen-bonded lead organic chalcogenolates (H-LOCs), offering an ideal platform for elucidating their structure–property relationships. By strategically functionalizing thiophenol with regiochemically or electronically distinct substituents, we achieved precise control at the ligand–ligand interface, yielding six distinct H-LOC architectures mediated by interlayer, intralayer, or cooperative hybrid hydrogen-bonding interactions. These programmed hydrogen-bonding interactions play an essential role in crystal growth, enabling the formation of large single crystals of two-dimensional (2D) LOCs. Combined structural and optical characterizations reveal a linear correlation between the ligand electronic effects and optical bandgaps of the materials, culminating in a narrow bandgap of 1.55 eV for the most electron-donating substituent. Most importantly, the reversible nature of these interfacial hydrogen bonds endows the H-LOCs with excellent solution-processability, allowing them to be fabricated into highly stable films with ambient durability exceeding two months─thereby unlocking their potential for optoelectronic devices.

title: Geometry-Programmed Connectivity Enables Predictive Assembly of Diamond-Family Colloidal Crystals
abstract: Abstract The predictive assembly of open colloidal crystals requires encoding specific connectivity rules into building blocks that are otherwise isotropic and lack inherent directionality. Here we introduce a geometry-programmed connectivity strategy in which spatial confinement, rather than surface patterning or lattice templating, programs not only particle coordination but also the accessible bonding arrangement that governs network connectivity. We implement this concept using tetrahedral DNA origami frameworks that confine DNA-functionalized spherical particles and restrict their accessible bonding pathways to four tetrahedrally arranged patches, thereby converting isotropic colloids into effective tetravalent building blocks with geometrically prescribed connectivity. A geometric hard-contact model translates these confinement-defined connectivity rules and the linker-defined interaction range into coordination regimes and lattice symmetry, yielding a predictive phase diagram. Guided by this model, we experimentally realize diamond-family colloidal crystals featuring the coexistence of cubic diamond and double diamond phases, as well as zinc blende and double zinc blende phases. Photonic band-structure calculations predict that the experimentally realized cubic diamond and zinc blende topologies can support complete PBGs in the deep-ultraviolet regime. We thus establish a predictive form of colloidal topological engineering, in which confinement geometry programs local connectivity and selects emergent crystal topology.

title: Buried CdSe Sacrificial Layer Driving Phase Evolution and Crystallization Kinetics Enables 14.78%‐Efficient DMF‐Based Kesterite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT During selenization, the inherent transport lag of Se from the film surface to the buried Mo/precursor interface causes early‐stage Se deficiency in the bottom region, creating a depth‐dependent crystallization lag that limits the homogeneity of Cu 2 ZnSn(S,Se) 4 (CZTSSe) absorbers. Here, we evaporate an ultrathin CdSe sacrificial layer at the Mo/precursor interface of N,N ‐dimethylformamide (DMF)‐derived CZTSSe absorbers. This layer is rapidly consumed at the onset of selenization, providing an in‐situ Se supply at the buried interface and effectively bypassing the intrinsic transport delay from the surface. The locally supplied Se initiates early‐stage bottom selenization and promotes the conversion of Cu 2 SnSe 3 ‐related intermediates toward CZTSSe while suppressing their persistent accumulation, enabling rear‐side nucleation and grain growth to commence substantially earlier than in the conventional surface‐dominated process. Meanwhile, the redistributed Cd 2+ partially substitutes Zn 2+ sites, reducing defect‐assisted recombination and enhancing carrier transport and extraction. The optimized device achieves a champion efficiency of 14.78% with a certified efficiency of 14.30%, establishing a new benchmark for DMF‐derived kesterite solar cells. This work demonstrates that prepositioning a sacrificial Se‐containing component at the buried interface to enable in situ release of Se offers a viable pathway for coordinating phase evolution and improving multinary chalcogenide absorber quality.

title: Adaptive Discovery of Uncharted Zeolitic Imidazolate Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Discovering new zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF) structures remains a major challenge because their assembly depends on the nature of the linker and synthesis conditions. Here, we introduce linker width as a design parameter for ZIF synthesis. We designed 4-substituted benzimidazole linkers with expanded width and combined them with smaller linkers in an adaptive machine-learning (ML) high-throughput strategy. This adaptive discovery scheme yielded nine new mixed-linker ZIFs, including six adopting the previously unrealized bcv topology. Single-crystal structural analysis reveals ordered linker distributions in which the wider 4-substituted benzimidazolate linkers code for the formation of 10-membered-ring needed for the apertures of the bcv cage. Comparison with representative mixed-linker ZIFs further identifies the width of linkers and the extension ratio as steric descriptors of topology selection. These results provide chemically interpretable design principles for mixed-linker ZIF assembly and demonstrate how linker design coupled with ML-guided synthesis can access unexplored regions of chemical space.

title: Operando Quantifying Li Plating Processes in Lithium‐Ion Pouch Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐ion batteries require high reliability and extended lifespan for practical grid storage applications, yet Li plating remains a critical hazard inducing rapid capacity fade and safety risks. The transient and heterogeneous nature of Li plating poses a significant challenge to real‐time quantitative detection. Herein, we define a critical Li‐plating areal capacity (q Li ) derived from dynamic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (DEIS) and establish an operando strategy to accurately quantify Li plating under diverse charging conditions. Validated by operando solid‐state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR)‐DEIS combined measurements, incremental capacity analysis, and mass spectrometry titration (MST), this method demonstrates high reliability, exceptional accuracy (R 2 > 0.97), and general validity across different temperatures (0°C–45°C) and battery capacities (4 to 110 mAh). A transmission line model (TLM) elucidates the physical origin of q Li : it corresponds to the critical surface coverage (∼10%, model‐derived) of lithium nuclei on graphite, marking the transition from nucleation‐dominated to growth‐controlled deposition. We further demonstrate that regulating temperature can switch the nucleation mode, thereby significantly altering q Li and the resulting plating characteristics. This study establishes a robust operando quantification platform, enabling early battery warning and adaptive fast charging to suppress excessive Li plating and extend service life in practical cells.

title: Guest Transition Metals in Host Keplerate Nanocapsules as Supramolecular Inorganic Functional Mimics of Monooxygenase Enzymes
abstract: ABSTRACT Advanced design of supramolecules can mimic enzyme complexes. Methane monooxygenases have several subparts, hydroxylases active for alkane oxidation, and complexes and channels that regulate electron, proton, substrate, and product access to the active site. The replication of a hydroxylase active site with inclusion of regulatory functionalities within a porous Keplerate nanocapsule host was undertaken. A Cu active site guest within a Keplerate cavity was prepared by an assembly reaction using a histidine surrogate as binding site for Cu II . The guest–host assembly enables transfer of protons and electrons and enables substrate and product diffusion to and from an active site into confined space. Characterization of the guest–host complex was by NMR, XPS, infrared, and Raman spectroscopies. Cyclic voltammetry was used to identify possible hydroxylase reactivity, followed by controlled potential electrolysis to verify hydrocarbon oxygenation. Substrate scope, optimal cathodic potential, and the number of metal sites needed were surveyed. Comparison of substrate reactivity revealed that their access to the active site was rate determining. Kinetics of a “dummy” substrate and product diffusion was measured by Guest Exchange Saturation Transfer 19 F NMR. These guest–host Keplerate nanocapsules represent an initial foray into the mimicking of a complicated metalloenzyme complex in an inorganic synthetic system.

title: Dimerization‐Enabled Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence and 500‐Fold Enhanced Emission in Gold Nanoclusters
abstract: ABSTRACT Gold nanoclusters (Au NCs) are promising luminescent materials with broad applications in sensing, bioimaging, and photonics. However, highly emissive thiolate‐protected Au NCs remain difficult to access because conformational relaxation of ligands and flexible Au–thiolate motifs often promote nonradiative relaxation. Herein, we show that dimerization can switch on thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) in non‐fluorescent Au NCs thus realizing the boost of quantum yield. Upon introduction of diphosphine ligands, Au 18 (SR) 14 undergoes assembly into a tethered dimer, (Au 18 )–(Au 2 S 3 )–(Au 18 ). This structural reorganization spatially separates the HOMO and LUMO over two Au 18 units, resulting in a small singlet–triplet energy gap (0.061 eV) and enabling reverse intersystem crossing. As a result, the non‐emissive monomer is converted into a highly emissive dimer with a photoluminescence quantum yield boosted from ∼0.1% to 50%. This work identifies dimerization as an effective strategy to activate the emission of dark NCs and establishes a design principle for TADF‐type metal nanoclusters.

title: Replacing CTAB with Renewable-Origin Surfactants for the Synthesis of Mesoporous 8YSZ: Structural Integrity, Functional Validation, and Sustainability Assessment
abstract: Abstract Cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB), a conventional structure-directing agent for mesoporous materials, is a petroleum-derived toxic compound whose removal requires energy-intensive multistep purification, increasing the environmental impact of the process. This study presents the sustainable synthesis of mesoporous 8 mol % yttria-stabilized zirconia (8YSZ) by replacing CTAB with glycerol (GLY) and glycerol monostearate (GMS), low-cost, renewable agents derived from the oleochemical industry. Raman spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, and N2 physisorption confirm the formation of fully cubic fluorite 8YSZ with mesoporous frameworks of interconnected nanocrystals, which exhibit appropriate macroporosity after high-temperature sintering. Ionic conductivity measurements, corrected for porosity, tortuosity, and constrictivity, demonstrate that scaffolds derived from renewable surfactants retain intrinsic oxygen-ion conduction equivalent to the CTAB reference and consistent with literature values for dense 8YSZ. A quantitative sustainability assessment shows that the renewable route reduces process mass intensity by up to 89% (from ∼710 to 78–81), energy intensity by 73% (from 3.87 to 1.03 kWh g–1), and production costs by up to 60%, while maintaining structural integrity in batches up to 10 g. These findings establish renewable surfactant substitution as a viable, scalable strategy for greener synthesis of functional porous ceramics, with direct relevance to electrochemical devices, catalyst substrates, and separation membranes.

title: Dual-Mode Exciton Coupling in Epitaxially Registered Organic–Inorganic 2D Heterocrystals
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) heterocrystals comprising molecules and semiconductors can serve as an ideal platform for studying interfacial excitons and for future optoelectronic applications, yet the energy and charge flow across these atomically sharp interfaces remain unclear. In this work, we investigated PTCDA/MoS2 as a prototypical 2D organic–inorganic heterostructure and revealed dual-mode exciton coupling between the constituent crystals. Monolayer-resolved PTCDA molecular crystals were grown on monolayer MoS2 via physical vapor assembly, and their crystallographic details, including the stacking angle, were determined by electron diffraction. Upon the formation of the heterostructures, PTCDA’s photoluminescence was nearly completely quenched by efficient interfacial excited-state decay, whereas that of MoS2 increased markedly with PTCDA thickness. Using differential reflectance and photoluminescence excitation (PLE) spectroscopy, we found that the enhancement arises from two distinct contributions. One contribution, observed without direct PTCDA excitation, is consistent with ground-state charge transfer injecting holes into MoS2, which suppresses negative trion formation and enhances the radiative recombination of neutral excitons. The other, correlated with PTCDA absorption in the PLE response, supports resonance energy transfer, which diverts excitation energy from PTCDA to MoS2. Our findings help reconcile previously proposed mechanisms and show how molecular and MoS2 excitonic responses evolve with molecular thickness in a structurally defined heterocrystal.

title: π‐Electronic Effects Dictate Interlayer Charge Transfer in Covalent Organic Frameworks With Boosted Photocatalytic Activity
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding interlayer charge transfer is central to the rational design of two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for high‐performance photocatalysis. Herein, we successfully modulate the interlayer charge transfer in donor–imine–donor type COFs by regulating the π‐electronic character of knots and linkers. We demonstrate that the rigid pyrene‐based knot with profound π‐electronic effect promotes efficient interlayer charge transfer, whereas the twisted biphenyl‐based counterpart effectively inhibits it combining with experimental and theoretical calculations. Specifically, the pyrene‐based units endow enhanced conjugation, improved planarity, and strengthened π–π stacking, giving rise to a substantially larger interlayer charge transfer amount for the fully rigid R–R–COF compared with the twisted T–T–COF. Consequently, R–R–COF achieves a superior H 2 evolution rate of 80.6 mmol g −1 h −1 , 89.6 times that of T–T–COF (0.9 mmol g −1 h −1 ) under identical conditions. Additionally, we reveal that topological selectivity correlates closely with the electronic nature of the knot. This work establishes π‐electronic effect as a key determinant of both interlayer charge transfer efficiency and photocatalytic activity, and provides a rational design strategy for advanced COF‐based photocatalysts.

title: Stable and selective C( sp 3)–H halogenation over COF-modified β -Fe2O3 photoanodes
abstract: Abstract Photoelectrocatalytic synthesis provides a sustainable route to high-value organic chemicals, yet achieving high selectivity while maintaining long-term stability remains challenging because of limited interfacial reactant availability and competing radical-mediated reaction pathways. Here, we develop a COF-modified photoanode by integrating a functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) onto β-Fe2O3 to regulate aqueous C(sp3)–H halogenation. Using cyclohexane chlorination as a model reaction, the COF-modified β-Fe2O3 photoanode achieves a monochlorination selectivity of up to 96.8% under AM 1.5 G illumination (100 mW cm−2), far exceeding the 53.9% obtained over bare β-Fe2O3. Under one-sun illumination, the photoanode delivers a photocurrent density of 2.8 mA cm−2 and remains stable for 300 h, retaining approximately 95% chlorocyclohexane selectivity at the end of the test. Even under 13-sun illumination, the photocurrent density reaches approximately 35 mA cm−2, with a chlorocyclohexane selectivity of 91.9% after 100 h. The COF-modified photoanode also shows enhanced monobromination and monoiodination selectivities, demonstrating the generality of this approach.

title: Engineering Synergistic Sites in a Cerium-Based Metal–Organic Framework for Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction
abstract: Abstract Photoreduction of CO2 to produce solar fuels is an important target. Redox-active Ce-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising catalysts. Herein, we have synthesized an amino-functionalized Ce-based MOF, PKU-167 (PKU = Peking University). Upon introduction of Co(bpy)2Cl2 (bpy = 2,2′-bipyridine) to the skeleton of PKU-167, PKU-167-0.9Co achieved a high CO production rate of 18.4 mmol g–1 h–1 with a selectivity of 91.8% under visible-light irradiation and an apparent quantum yield of 1.97% at 425 nm. In situ characterizations and modeling reveal a synergistic adsorption–reduction mechanism, where amino groups enrich adsorption of CO2 for subsequent photoreduction on {Ce6} clusters and Co2+ sites in concert to achieve the optimal photocatalytic performance. This study will advance the rational design of redox-active Ce-based MOFs as efficient photocatalysts.

title: In Situ X‐Ray Scattering Reveals the Nucleation, Growth, and Self‐Assembly of CsBr Nanocrystals in a Heterogeneous Medium
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how nanocrystals form is central to the rational synthesis of nanomaterials, yet the formation mechanisms of ionic nanocrystals remain poorly resolved. Here, we use synchrotron‐based in situ small‐ and wide‐angle X‐ray scattering to track the formation and assembly of CsBr nanocrystals in solution. We find that the precursors spontaneously organize into dense clusters before reaction, generating a heterogeneous reaction medium that dictates the subsequent formation pathway. Following injection of Cs‐oleate, these clusters act as metastable precursor reservoirs that regulate precursor availability, thereby sustaining extended nucleation and promoting effective size focusing. At later stages, the same clusters function as depletants that drive the self‐assembly of CsBr nanocrystals into face‐centered cubic superlattices. These superlattices then undergo partial disassembly through Ostwald ripening, governed by the interplay between structural ordering and kinetic evolution. Together, our results identify multiple roles of precursor clusters during nanocrystal formation and assembly and provide mechanistic insights into ionic nanocrystal synthesis in heterogeneous media.

title: Quantum Sensing of Lithium Ions with Defect-Engineered Recognition Pockets in a TEMPO-Modified Covalent Organic Framework
abstract: Abstract Nuclear-spin quantum sensing requires coherent molecular electron spin qubits embedded in analyte-recognizing local environments that bring target nuclei into their short-range hyperfine detection volume. Here, we introduce TA-TEMPO, a covalent organic framework in which dilute nitroxide radicals and Li+-binding triazine moieties form defect-engineered recognition pockets for room-temperature 7Li sensing. Optimizing radical density preserves spin coherence while maximizing the 7Li/1H response acquired by hyperfine spectroscopy. TA-TEMPO detects Li+ in a tetrahydrofuran solution of LiBr with a sensitivity of 1.0 × 10–4 mol·L–1 at room temperature, a 50-fold improvement over the previous benchmark, and enables quantum sensing across several lithium-based electrolytes. Control experiments and density functional theory calculations show that triazine sites preferentially bind Li+ over Na+ and position it near nitroxide radicals, accounting for selective detection in a large excess of Na+. These results establish chemically programmed host–guest recognition as a strategy to integrate sensitivity, selectivity, and coherent spin readout in porous molecular quantum sensors.

title: Accessing Core-Functionalized DNA–Polymer Nanostructures via RAFT Polymerization-Induced Self-Assembly
abstract: Abstract DNA–polymer nanostructures with precise sequences and programmable recognition capabilities are capable of achieving spatially accurate organization of functional moieties for applications in targeted drug delivery, biosensing, bioimaging, and regenerative medicine. However, traditional synthetic routes for DNA–polymer nanostructures are cumbersome and inefficient, while existing RAFT-PISA systems are restricted to limited monomer types, leading to insufficient core functionality and poor property adjustability. Herein, we present the fabrication of core-functionalized DNA–polymer nanostructures via RAFT-PISA of a thymine-containing monomer in both DMF/water mixed solvent and pure water. Efficient and well-controlled polymerization is achieved by using a DNA-modified chain transfer agent (CTA); however, dense surface DNA chains inhibit structural evolution to form only spherical aggregates. Tuning the surface DNA density and adopting hydrophilic macromolecular CTA enable successful access to spheres, worms, and vesicles by simply regulating core chain lengths. The newly developed core-functionalized DNA–polymer nanostructures retain excellent DNA recognition capability in the shell layer. Meanwhile, they allow programmable post-polymerization morphology modulation through multiple hydrogen bonds in the core layer. This strategy not only provides a reliable approach to constructing distinct DNA–polymer nanostructures but also expands and advances PISA toward tunable core-functionalized nano-objects.

title: Magnetic Ordering Controlled by Ionic Proximity in Self-Assembled Ionic Liquid Nanostructures
abstract: Abstract Magnetic ionic liquids (MILs) commonly exhibit paramagnetic behavior because the spatially isolated and disordered arrangement of magnetic centers limits cooperative magnetic interactions. Herein, the terphenyl-based MIL 3ph-imi[FeCl4] was processed under different conditions to obtain three samples with distinct structural organizations. Liquid-nitrogen quenching produced an amorphous solid. Aging a 1.0 mg mL–1 aqueous solution at 25 °C yielded 50–90 nm spindle-shaped assemblies (Assembly-1) containing locally ordered domains, whereas aging at 5 °C generated ca. 40 μm platelets (Assembly-2) with lamellar periodicity and extended in-plane crystalline order. Magnetic measurements showed predominantly paramagnetic behavior for 3ph-imi[FeCl4]. Assembly-1 exhibited weak magnetic hysteresis at 5 K and zero-field-cooled/field-cooled (ZFC–FC) bifurcation below ca. 42 K. In contrast, Assembly-2 showed ZFC–FC bifurcation below ca. 258 K and retained a distinct hysteresis loop at 300 K. The compact molecular packing of the assembled samples may strengthen interactions among neighboring [FeCl4]− units, while the higher structural order and greater spatial continuity of Assembly-2 may support magnetic correlations across larger regions and over a wider temperature range. These findings demonstrate that temperature-regulated aqueous self-assembly provides an effective strategy for tuning the solid-state magnetic properties of small-molecule MILs.

title: LinkerGen: Guided Autoregressive Generation of Organic Linkers for Reticular Chemistry
abstract: Organic linker design for reticular materials requires balancing molecular diversity with structural and chemical constraints. Here, we introduce LinkerGen, a compact SMILES-based autoregressive model guided by chemical building unit (CBU) types, numerical property targets, or text descriptions. We train and evaluate two model sizes on approximately 22 million fragment-enumerated carboxylate linkers spanning 2-linear, 2-bent, and 3-planar CBU types. Model size and sampling temperature adjust the balance between validity and novelty, while conditioning increases the yield of distinct, valid, novel candidates satisfying selected requests compared with unconditioned generation followed by filtering. Text conditioning combines molecular requirements in a single natural-language request, although its effectiveness depends on training coverage and prompt formulation. A prospective application connects literature-informed linker generation to metal–organic polyhedron (MOP) assembly and calculated binding energies for 5-fluorouracil, illustrating how chemical design hypotheses can be explored through computational screening. LinkerGen provides a steerable source of candidate building units and a basis for adaptation to other linker families and design objectives through suitable training data and conditioning information. Highlights • Generative model for reticular organic chemical building units (CBUs) widen the chemical linker space available for the design of metal-organic polyhedra. • Conditioning enriches generated populations in linkers with desired properties. • Text conditioning allows complex chemical requirements to be effectively expressed in natural language.

title: CoO Nanoislands as Metal Oxide Precursors for Surface-Supported Co–BDA Coordination Networks
abstract: Metal oxide nanoislands offer a localized source of metal centers for the on-surface assembly of coordination networks. Here, we investigate the adsorption and thermal evolution of 4,4'-biphenyldicarboxylic acid (BDA) on CoO nanoislands supported on Au(111) under ultrahigh vacuum using infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy (IRAS), scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), and density functional theory (DFT). At 400 K, BDA forms two coexisting populations: carboxylate species anchored to CoO and a predominantly flat-lying, hydrogen-bonded molecular layer on Au(111). Heating to 500 K removes the IR signatures of intact carboxylic acid groups and changes the relative intensities of the out-of-plane C-H modes. STM reveals a rectangular two-dimensional Co–BDA coordination network, for which DFT supports a structural model containing paired Co centers. These observations support a pathway in which Co species are supplied by partial dissolution of the oxide nanoislands. Annealing to 600 K produces arrays of coordination chains with single-Co nodes, while the IR spectra remain consistent with predominantly flat-lying biphenyl units. These results demonstrate that supported metal oxide nanoislands can serve as precursors for the formation of surface-confined 2D MOFs and provide an alternative route to thermally controlled metal–organic assembly on metal surfaces. TOC Graphic Thermally controlled MOF growth. CoO nanoislands on Au(111) serve as a metal precursor for the formation of a surface-confined Co–BDA network. Annealing at 500 K produces a rectangular 2D MOF with paired Co centers, while further annealing to 600 K induces a transformation into 1D Co–BDA arrays with single-Co nodes. This oxide-mediated approach provides a new route to surface-supported 2D MOF synthesis.

title: Guest-Assisted Assembled Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks of Dysprosium Single-Ion Magnets
abstract: Abstract Lanthanide single-ion magnets (Ln-SIMs) have gradually emerged as one of the important candidates for next-generation magnetic materials. However, improving the environmental stability of Ln-SIMs remains one of the key challenges. Herein, we present a strategy for preparing highly thermostable Ln-SIMs through guest-assisted assembly of Ln-SIM-based hydrogen bonded organic frameworks (HOFs). Two HOFs based on Ln-SIMs, [HGdn]2[Dy(dpa)2(Hdpa)]·0.5Gdn·H2O (HOF-1) and [Dy(Hdpa)3]2·3H2O (HOF-2), have been prepared, where Gdn and H2dpa represent guanidine and pyridine-2,6-dicarboxylic acid, respectively. HOF-1 is constructed from [Dy(dpa)2(Hdpa)]2- anions and [HGdn]+ cations, giving rise to a three-dimensional HOF structure. HOF-2 consists of [Dy(Hdpa)3] units linked by guest H2O molecules to form a two-dimensional HOF. Both HOF-1 and HOF-2 exhibit excellent thermal stability. They can maintain their frameworks above 290 °C and thus rank among the most thermally stable Ln-SIMs reported to date. They also exhibit field-induced dual magnetic relaxation behaviors, with the highest effective energy barriers (Ueff) of 61.4 K (HOF-1) and 61.5 K (HOF-2), respectively. This work presents a novel approach for enhancing the structural stability of Ln-SIMs and regulating their magnetic properties through a guest-assisted assembly strategy for supramolecular HOF structures.

title: Scalable Room-Temperature Synthesis of Glass-like MOF Thin Films on Arbitrary Substrates with Versatile Functionality
abstract: Metal-organic framework (MOF) glasses and glass-like materials offer unique advantages including improved flexibility, processability and mechanical stability, yet the rational, mild and scalable synthesis of uniform, large-area glassy MOF thin films remains largely unexplored and highly challenging. Herein, we pioneer the fabrication of homogeneous, ultra-smooth glass-like MOF thin films, which can be readily scaled into large-area coatings via a facile room-temperature immersion strategy. By simply placing diverse substrates into the precursor solution for 0.5 to 3 hours, continuous amorphous MOF films with nanometer-scale flatness and centimeter-to-0.3-meter scale uniformity can be readily prepared, with exceptional mechanical properties including Young’s modulus among the highest reported for typical ZIF glasses. Importantly, this unprecedented glass-like MOF film serves as a versatile guiding layer that enables the nucleation and growth of 15 different types of crystalline MOFs on various substrates, overcoming long-standing limitations of substrate dependence and lattice mismatch. This work not only establishes a facile and scalable synthetic platform for high-performance glass-like MOF thin films, but also extends its capability toward the universal growth of crystalline MOF films, unlocking promising new opportunities for device-oriented MOF thin-film materials for gas and isotope separation, electronic devices, sensing and electrocatalytic applications.

title: Multifunctional 2D Polymeric Nanofiber Networks via Proton-Mediated Assembly for High-Temperature Applications
abstract: Abstract Advanced heat-resistant nanofibrous networks are attracting growing attention as critical functional components owing to thermostable porous architectures and selective sieving capabilities that offer reliable safeguards and a technical foundation to ensure safe operation and sophisticated manufacturing in harsh thermal environments. However, the high glass transition temperature and narrow processing window of heat-resistant polymers limit processing accuracy, making it difficult to achieve nanoscale processing of fibers and regulation of their assembled architectures, thereby causing a conflict between the heat resistance advantage and structural functionalization. Here, we report a universal proton-mediated intermolecular interaction regulation strategy for regulating the self-assembly pathway and morphology of heat-resistant nanofibers without dependence on melting or dissolution, to fabricate two-dimensional (2D) thermally reliable nanofiber networks (TR-nets) with fine separation function. By customizing the nanofiber dispersion properties and electrospraying process parameters, we couple the assembly of nanofibers mediated by proton transfer with the 2D deformation of nanofiber dispersion microdroplets sprayed from a Taylor cone, thereby manipulating the dominant intermolecular interactions to dynamically switch between repulsion and attraction in the 2D plane, regulating the topological assembly behavior of nanofiber building blocks. Benefiting from the hydrophobic porous Steiner network architecture and intrinsic material thermal stability, the fabricated TR-nets exhibit multifunctionality combining liquid repellency, air permeability, dust prevention, and sound transmission, and can withstand high-temperature environments up to 400 °C. This work may afford innovative perspectives for the advanced design and development of functionally integrated devices capable of working in high-temperature environments.

title: Physicochemical Prioritization of Hypothetical Metal–Organic Frameworks for Experimental Synthesis
abstract: The rapid expansion of AI-driven and computationally designed metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) raises a fundamental question: which hypothetical structures are most likely to be experimentally realized? Here, we develop a physicochemically informed strategy to prioritize MOFs for synthesis by integrating molecular synthetic accessibility, framework geometry, electronic structure, solvent removal stability, and thermodynamic stability through positive–unlabeled learning. Using 9,033 experimentally reported MOFs as examples of realized structures and hypothetical MOFs as candidates with unknown synthesizability, we identify 5 complementary physicochemical descriptors that enable effective prioritization, achieving a source-averaged normalized positive rank of 0.93 by placing experimentally realized MOFs near the top of candidate rankings across held-out database sources. Further analysis reveals that experimentally realized MOFs are enriched at low linker geometric distortion and low energy above the convex hull of competing phases, highlighting complementary geometric and thermodynamic considerations. Moreover, secondary building unit–linker analyses identify specific chemical combinations enriched among highly ranked hypothetical structures. Together, these findings establish a chemically interpretable approach to prioritizing hypothetical MOFs and help bridge the gap between computational materials design and experimental synthesis.

title: Mechanically Tunable Quantum Transport in Graphene Nanoribbons with Antiaromatic Motifs
abstract: Abstract Nonbenzenoid graphene nanoribbons provide a versatile platform for tailoring electronic structures beyond conventional benzenoid π-conjugated systems, yet the impact of their topology on quantum transport remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate electrical conductance through suspended ladder phenylene nanoribbons containing antiaromatic four-membered rings using scanning tunneling microscope lifting spectroscopy. As the nanoribbon is progressively detached from the substrate, differential conductance measurements reveal successive charge-state transitions accompanied by alternating Kondo resonances, demonstrating the dynamic generation of localized spins in an intrinsically closed-shell nanoribbon. Density functional theory calculations show that the antiaromatic topology reduces the HOMO–LUMO gap and induces a pronounced length dependence of the occupied frontier orbitals, which shift progressively toward and eventually across the electrode Fermi level with increasing suspended length, driving successive charge-state transitions. The transport behavior is quantitatively described within a double-barrier tunneling framework incorporating charge quantization and many-body interactions. These results suggest an antiaromaticity-driven mechanism for charge-state evolution and propose antiaromaticity as a molecular design principle for controlling charge and spin states in nonbenzenoid carbon nanostructures.

title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Synthesis of Multisubstituted Conjugated Dienes from Unactivated Alkenes
abstract: ABSTRACT The efficient and stereoselective synthesis of multisubstituted conjugated 1,3‐dienes remains a longstanding challenge because of the difficulty in controlling regioselectivity and stereochemistry. In this study, we report a ligand‐promoted, carboxylate‐directed palladium‐catalyzed alkenylation of unactivated alkenes with vinyl iodides for the modular synthesis of multisubstituted conjugated 1,3‐dienes. A bulky norbornane‐based monophosphine ligand (NBphos) is key to overcoming the intrinsically low reactivity and poor regiocontrol of unactivated alkenes, enabling efficient coupling with high regio‐ and stereoselectivity. The protocol provides access to a broad range of multisubstituted 1,3‐dienes, including highly congested pentasubstituted derivatives. Notably, stereodivergent synthesis of either diene stereoisomer is achieved directly from the corresponding E ‐ or Z ‐configured alkene substrates. The synthetic utility of the method is demonstrated through the derivatization of glycals and diverse downstream Diels–Alder transformations. Mechanistic studies reveal that a free carboxylic acid is indispensable for directing the palladium‐catalyzed alkenylation, underscoring the critical role of substrate coordination in achieving the observed reactivity and selectivity.

title: Porphyrin Integration Enhances Bipolar Redox Accessibility for High‐Rate Sodium‐Based Dual‐Ion Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Closing the gap between theoretical multielectron capacity and practical accessibility remains the central bottleneck for high‐energy organic batteries. Herein, we report a molecular design strategy that integrates a porphyrin motif into a sulfur‐rich conjugated polymer (BTTP) to align electronic structure, state‐dependent ion interactions, and electrochemical kinetics across the bipolar window. Despite possessing a lower theoretical capacity than its reference counterpart (BTB), BTTP achieves an exceptional theoretical capacity utilization of 94.2% (delivering 477 mAh g −1 at 0.5 A g −1 , compared to only 53.5% and 351 mAh g −1 for BTB). Electrokinetic analyses, including GITT and DRT, confirm accelerated apparent ion diffusion and reduced polarization limitations, enabling BTTP to retain 166 mAh g −1 at an ultrahigh current density of 20 A g −1 over 25 000 cycles. Operando/ex situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations elucidate that the dual pyrrolic/imino nitrogen sites in porphyrin and the sulfur‐rich backbone cooperatively provide potential‐dependent coordination environments for PF 6 − anions and Na + cations. This work suggests that molecular regulation of complementary ion‐interaction environments within multi‐active‐unit frameworks, rather than simply increasing the number of redox units, is important for enhancing rate capability and capacity utilization.

title: PASS‐Derived O/S Donor Field‐Directed Competitive–Cooperative Fe/Co Phase Evolution for Cross‐Band Microwave Absorption
abstract: ABSTRACT Fe/Co bimetallic regulation enables high‐performance microwave absorbers, yet the role of intrinsic coordination disparity in precursor conversion, nonequilibrium phase evolution, and cross‐band loss redistribution remains unclear. We design a poly(arylene sulfide sulfone) (PASS)‐predefined O/S heterogeneous donor‐field strategy to direct competitive–cooperative nonequilibrium phase evolution in Fe/Co systems. Covalently embedded sulfone‐O and thioether‐S sites, with PASS's rigid backbone, create a molecularly preorganized donor field that amplifies non‐equivalent Fe/Co coordination, promoting competitive bonding, differentiated phase pathways, and electronic‐state reconstruction during confined pyrolysis. Fe/Co regulation thus reshapes local phases, O/S chemical environments, and interfacial charge states via Fe─O/Co─S coordination preferences, generating multiphase heterostructures, amorphous/crystalline interfaces, defects, and lattice strain while balancing dielectric polarization, conductive transport, magnetic response, and impedance matching. The resulting CFC absorber achieves cross‐band absorption in low‐frequency 5G and high‐frequency radar bands. CFC‐4 exhibits −73.83 dB at 6.23 GHz (3.20 mm) and −76.59 dB at 16.98 GHz (1.31 mm), with a maximum EAB of 5.03 GHz. CFC‐4∼6 (1–5 mm) show >90% cumulative effective absorption over 2–18 GHz. Finite‐element simulations reveal a maximum RCS reduction of 42.5 dB on PEC. This work establishes O/S donor‐field engineering as a viable route to amplify Fe/Co coordination differentiation for efficient cross‐band microwave absorption.

title: Sulfur Locking and Chlorination Synergistically Enable Efficient Charge Transport and Low Nonradiative Energy Loss in Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving efficient charge transport while maintaining low nonradiative energy loss remains a key challenge in the molecular design of small‐molecule acceptors (SMAs) for organic solar cells (OSCs). Herein, we report a stepwise molecular engineering strategy based on sulfur locking and chlorination to regulate intermolecular packing and excited‐state properties simultaneously. Sulfur locking modifies molecular conformation and intermolecular packing, leading to enhanced exciton diffusion and charge transport. Subsequent chlorination further strengthens intermolecular interactions through additional Cl···S contacts, resulting in tighter π–π stacking and improved crystalline ordering. Binary OSCs based on D18:Qx2Ph‐SCl achieve an efficiency of 20.0% with a high open‐circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 0.951 V, while maintaining a low nonradiative energy loss of ∼0.19 eV. Owing to its intrinsically lower reorganization energy and weaker electron–phonon coupling than L8‐BO, Qx2Ph‐SCl further serves as an effective third component in ternary OSCs, reducing nonradiative recombination and increasing the V OC . As a result, the ternary device delivers an efficiency of 21.3%. This work demonstrates that stepwise sulfur locking and chlorination provide an effective molecular design strategy for simultaneously optimizing charge transport and voltage loss in high‐performance OSCs.

title: Stepwise Fusion Kinetics in Block Copolymer Micelles: Effect of Solvent Quality for the Corona
abstract: Abstract Block copolymer micelles in the strongly segregated regime are often trapped in nonequilibrium states, with large barriers to re-arrangement. Here, we show that micelle fusion can be induced, and its onset tuned, by controlling the solvent quality for the corona block. Small, kinetically trapped polystyrene-block-poly(ethylene oxide) (PS-PEO) micelles were prepared in two ionic liquids ([C4mim][BF4] and [C6mim][BF4]) and their mixtures, in which the PEO corona exhibits lower critical solution temperature phase behavior. Upon heating, synchrotron small-angle X-ray scattering and static light scattering reveal that the micelles grow irreversibly in discrete steps, as the second virial coefficient for PEO in the solvent approaches zero and even changes sign. The characteristic step temperatures vary linearly with the solvent composition, demonstrating that the onset of fusion is dictated by the corona–solvent interaction. A second-order kinetic model with an Arrhenius rate constant quantitatively describes the first fusion step and yields a large apparent activation energy of ca. 185 kJ/mol, independent of solvent composition. These results establish solvent quality for the corona as a key parameter regulating the fusion of kinetically trapped micelles and provide a general strategy for directing block copolymer assemblies toward equilibrium.

title: Pore Engineering of IL@MOF-Derived Carbons via IL-Assisted Double Templating for CO2 Separation
abstract: Abstract The mitigation of carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions requires adsorbent materials with tunable pore structures capable of balancing adsorption capacity and selectivity under postcombustion conditions. In this work, a proof-of-concept IL-assisted double-templating strategy is presented to engineer porosity in IL@MOF-derived carbons. The metal–organic framework (MOF) Cu-BTC was used as both carbon precursor and primary template, while the ionic liquid (IL) [C6MIM][B(CN)4] was used as a secondary sacrificial template at low loadings (1–10 wt %). IL@MOF composites with varying IL contents were prepared, carbonized, and subsequently acid-washed to remove residual copper-containing phases formed during carbonization. This enabled the evaluation of how IL loading influences the resulting carbon pore structure and adsorption behavior. Porosimetric characterization shows that IL incorporation promoted the development of additional (ultra)microporosity while simultaneously reducing total accessible pore volume at higher loadings, strongly influencing gas adsorption behavior. CO2 and N2 adsorption–desorption measurements at 303 K revealed a nonmonotonic dependence of CO2 adsorption capacity on IL loading, with a maximum at 2 wt % IL. At higher IL contents, the reduction in accessible pore volume limited adsorption capacity. In contrast, ideal CO2/N2 selectivity at 1 bar increased progressively with IL loading. These results show that even small amounts of IL can systematically tune pore architecture and adsorption performance in IL@MOF-derived carbons. Overall, IL-assisted double templating was validated as a versatile approach for pore engineering in carbon adsorbents, providing a framework for the rational design of materials for CO2 separation applications.

title: Controlling Polymorphism and Particle Size in Zr‐Based Metal‐Organic Frameworks Through Preformed Nodes and Machine‐Learning‐Assisted Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Framework topology and particle size jointly govern pore architecture, diffusion limitations, and accessible surface area, making their simultaneous control essential for functional metal–organic framework (MOF) design. Achieving reproducible control over both remains a central challenge in MOF chemistry, particularly for systems capable of crystallizing in multiple polymorphs. Here, we systematically explore the synthesis of two Zr‐based MOFs, NU‐1000 and NU‐901, which share the same Zr 6 ‐oxo cluster and pyrene‐tetrabenzoate linker but differ in topology. To remove variability arising from in situ precursor formation, we employed preformed Zr 6 ‐oxo clusters as well‐defined nodes. Building on this controlled starting point, multiple particle‐size regimes (<100 nm to ∼1 µm) were accessed through systematic variation of modulator identity and loading, co‐modulator content, linker equivalents, temperature, and dilution. Machine‐learning (ML) analysis quantitatively disentangles the multivariate influences governing phase selection and particle‐size evolution. This integrated approach enables predictive navigation of the synthesis parameter space, providing reproducible access to MOFs with defined size regimes and controlled topology. Together, these results establish a generalizable experimental‐computational workflow that transforms empirical MOF synthesis into a predictable, designable process, enabling rational control over polymorphism and growth in structurally adaptable framework materials.

title: Hexafluoroethane purification via molecular sieving in a molecule-trap metal-organic framework
abstract: Purification of hexafluoroethane (C2F6) from ternary mixtures containing hydrofluorocarbons (C2H2F4 and C2HF5) using conventional routes is energy-intensive. Here, we report C2F6 purification through shape-selective molecular sieving in a molecular-trap metal-organic framework enabled by isoreticular pore-geometry tuning. Starting from PCP-FDCA, we constructed BUT-313 by a minimal O-to-S substitution in the dicarboxylate linker. This single-atom edit transforms the original rectangular channel into an hourglass-like bottlenecked pore with a narrowed constriction of 4.2 Å. As a result, BUT-313 strongly suppresses the uptake of the more symmetric C2F6 while still adsorbing the anisotropic fluorocarbons C2H2F4 and C2HF5. At 298 K and 100 kPa, BUT-313 exhibits the highest uptake ratios of 7.7 for C2H2F4/C2F6 and 6.0 for C2HF5/C2F6, together with a record-high C2H2F4/C2F6 selectivity of 487.0. In ternary breakthrough experiments, BUT-313 delivers >99.98% C2F6 with a productivity of 184.5 L/kg, while retaining its performance over multiple cycles and after scale-up to the 10 g level. By replacing oxygen with sulfur in a MOF linker, researchers reshaped rectangular pores into hourglass bottlenecks, switching separation from thermodynamic to geometry-driven sieving. BUT-313 achieves C2H2F4/C2F6 selectivity of 487.0 and purifies >99.98% C2F6 from ternary mixtures, with stable performance after 10-g scale-up and cycling.

title: Crystallization‐Driven Self‐Assembly of Polymers and Emerging Technologies
abstract: ABSTRACT Crystallization plays an important role in polymer self‐assembly by directing molecular packing, internal ordering, and morphology regulation. The emergence of crystallization‐driven self‐assembly (CDSA) has provided a powerful strategy for constructing polymer nanostructures with controlled dimensions, anisotropic morphologies, and desired functions. This review focuses on the CDSA of polymers and emerging technologies, with emphasis on the mechanistic roles of crystallization in nucleation and growth, as well as the regulation of their morphology and functions by molecular design and external parameters such as concentration, solvent, temperature, light, and pH. We also summarize representative characterization methods and simulations used to reveal the CDSA of polymers, and highlight potential applications in biomedicine, optoelectronics, anti‐counterfeiting, information storage, and catalysis. Finally, current challenges and future opportunities in CDSA and emerging strategies are discussed.

title: Small-Molecule-Mediated Molecular Recognition Controls Tryptophan Self-Assembly and Programs Tunable Emission
abstract: Abstract Engineering fluorescence from natural biomolecules without covalent modification offers a sustainable route to functional optical materials, yet biomolecule-based optical materials remain relatively unexplored, and the molecular principles governing their emergent photophysics remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that small-molecule-directed self-assembly can redirect tryptophan (Trp) from uncontrolled fibrillar aggregation toward well-defined supramolecular architectures while tuning its intrinsic fluorescence through distinct molecular- and solvent-mediated pathways. Co-assembly with l-ascorbic acid (Asc, pH ∼ 3) suppresses the native Trp emission (∼350 nm) and generates a band at 470 nm (λex = 380 nm), showing a remarkable 120 nm red-shift, with a fluorescence quantum yield (ϕ) of 0.13. This process produces spherical assemblies (∼12.5 μm) through first-order kinetics, driven by π–π stacking, hydrogen bonding, and CH−π interactions. These stable assemblies exhibit reversible pH-responsive emission and reduced cytotoxicity compared to conventional dyes. In contrast, hydrazine (Hyd, pH 10) accelerates assembly formation by ∼2.5-fold, yielding larger spheres (∼18 μm) with emission centered at 430 nm (λex = 345 nm), exhibiting a 40 nm blue shift relative to Trp-Asc assemblies. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal distinct molecular mechanisms: Asc directly associates with Trp, whereas Hyd preferentially reorganizes the surrounding water network, indicating a predominantly solvent-controlled pathway for reorganization and association. Metadynamics further reveals that Hyd reshapes the Trp–Trp association landscape, favoring a specific geometry over tighter packing. Thus, small-molecule-mediated control over molecular recognition, solvation, and intermolecular organization can redirect uncontrolled biomolecular aggregation into defined supramolecular architectures while programming emergent fluorescence, establishing a noncovalent strategy for engineering supramolecular fluorophores from native biomolecules.

title: Discrete and Interlocked Metal–Organic Cages: A Rationally Designed Laboratory Platform for Investigating Self-Assembly and the Conversion of Kinetic to Thermodynamic Supramolecular Complexes
abstract: Abstract In this two-part undergraduate laboratory experiment, students synthesize a bis(pyridyl) ligand and subsequently investigate its coordination-driven self-assembly using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy within a problem-based inquiry framework. The reaction of the ligand with palladium(II) ions in acetonitrile at a 2:1 stoichiometric ratio gives rise to two distinct cage architectures: a kinetically favored M2L4 assembly and a thermodynamically stable interlocked M4L8 complex, with their relative distributions governed by reaction conditions. This experiment not only develops essential experimental skills but also reinforces key concepts spanning organic synthesis, coordination chemistry, and chemical thermodynamics. The modular design and operational simplicity make it readily adaptable to a wide range of undergraduate curricula.

title: Mixed Thiolate/Alkoxide Antimony Cages for Reversed-Bilayer Vesicle Self-Assembly and Dye Protection in Organic Media
abstract: A new two-step synthesis produces moisture-stable antimony and arsenic dithiothreitol cages. Structural analysis reveals that the Sb compounds self-assemble into reversed bilayers, consistent with pnictogen-bonded vesicle formation in organic media. The Sb assemblies more efficiently encapsulate and protect rhodamine B than the arsenic analogue or a topological mimic that lacks pnictogen-bonding capability. This work provides a synthetically accessible tool for partitioning organic media to allow for orthogonal reactivity.

title: Photoactive Heterometallic Assemblies Based on Dinuclear Clathrochelate Metalloligands and a ZnII–Porphyrin/RuII–Metallacycle
abstract: Abstract A modular self-assembly strategy combining a RuII-metallacycle of ZnII-porphyrins with three different dinuclear boron-capped clathrochelate metalloligands bearing two hexacoordinate metal ions in the center (either ZnII/ZnII or mixed-valence FeII/FeIII cores) affords a new family of discrete photoactive heterometallic sandwich-like assemblies. The assemblies are formed quantitatively in solution and fully characterized by UV–Vis, IR, and NMR spectroscopy, DOSY, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. The nature of the intercomponent photoinduced process depends critically on the identity of the clathrochelate connector: in the ZnII/ZnII-containing assembly, excitation of the clathrochelate unit results in quantitative energy transfer to the ZnII-porphyrin platform; in the FeII/FeIII-containing assembly, the ZnII-porphyrin singlet excited state is completely quenched by the mixed-valence iron core. These results demonstrate that the photoinduced intercomponent process can be switched simply by varying the metal identity within the clathrochelate connector, while retaining the same overall supramolecular architecture, offering a new design principle for photoactive multicomponent inorganic assemblies.

title: Water Rolls Off, Current Flows: The Rise of Conductive Superhydrophobic Textiles
abstract: ABSTRACT Conductive superhydrophobic textiles uniquely combine electrical conductivity with extreme water repellency, enabling humidity‐resistant wearable electronics, smart protective clothing, and self‐powered systems. This review systematically examines the design principles, fabrication strategies, and multifunctional applications of these materials, with a focus on the core interfacial coupling mechanism—water rolls off, current flows—that governs their performance. Key application domains are critically analyzed, with emphasis on how superhydrophobic protection enhances device stability under humid, sweaty, or rainy conditions. The review identifies fundamental bottlenecks—conductive network failure under deformation, poor durability of hydrophobic interfaces, and inherent trade‐offs between conductivity and water repellency—that currently limit practical deployment. A structured translation roadmap from laboratory design to scalable manufacturing is presented, incorporating the development workflow of discovery, design, fabrication, testing, validation, qualification, scaling, deployment, impact, and sustainability. Future directions, including stretchable self‐healing architectures, artificial intelligence (AI)‐guided inverse design, fluorine‐free sustainable manufacturing, and self‐powered wireless textile systems, are discussed with technical specificity. This review provides a unified framework connecting materials chemistry, textile engineering, and device physics, guiding researchers and engineers toward transforming these materials from laboratory prototypes to real‐world products that enhance human safety, comfort, and connectivity.
